jobs.description: Employer: Concrete Strategies Expires: 11/13/2026 Layout Engineer Intern CONCRETE STRATEGIES - Nationwide, USA, United StatesTagged: InternshipAs a Layout Engineer Intern at Concrete Strategies, you'll be immersed in the critical aspect of translating design plans into real-world construction. Your role involves mastering the art of precise measurements, spatial alignment, and layout implementation to ensure the accurate placement of structures and components on the construction site.During your internship, you'll have the opportunity to learn about and contribute to:Blueprint Interpretation: Learn to interpret architectural and engineering blueprints, understanding the spatial relationships and dimensions depicted in the plans. Learn to use 2D and 3D CAD models for robotic construction layout.Site Preparation: Assist in preparing the construction site for layout activities, ensuring that the area is ready for accurate measurements and positioning.Measurement Techniques: Gain expertise in using surveying equipment, laser levels, and other tools to take precise measurements and establish reference points.Spatial Alignment: Collaborate with experienced layout engineers to ensure that structures, foundations, and key components align with the design plans.Layout Implementation: Participate in translating design dimensions onto the actual construction site, marking key points and lines for construction activities.Quality Control: Engage in quality checks to verify the accuracy of layout measurements, ensuring that they adhere to project specifications.Coordination: Work closely with project managers and construction teams to ensure seamless communication and alignment during the layout process.Problem Solving: Contribute to finding solutions when discrepancies arise between design plans and on-site conditions, helping to maintain project integrity.Data Recording: Maintain accurate records of layout activities, measurements, and adjustments made during the construction process.Professional Development: Engage in learning opportunities to enhance your understanding of layout engineering techniques and tools.Concrete Strategies places great importance on precise layout engineering to ensure the successful execution of construction projects. This internship experience will provide you with valuable skills and insights, preparing you for a rewarding career in construction layout engineering.QualificationsCurrently pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.Familiarity with construction layout techniques, instruments, and software.Proficiency in using AutoCAD, Total Station, and other relevant tools.Ability to interpret project plans, blueprints, and specifications for accurate layout implementation.Meticulous attention to detail to ensure precise measurements and alignment.Clear verbal and written communication skills for effective collaboration with project teams.Willingness to troubleshoot layout challenges and find solutions on-site.Collaborative attitude, capable of working closely with other team members, contractors, and stakeholders.Effective time management skills to meet layout deadlines within project schedules.Ability to work on construction sites, often requiring standing, walking, and working outdoors.About Concrete StrategiesConcrete Strategies is the nation’s leading full-service, design-build, turnkey concrete contractor. Concrete Strategies employs over 1,300 field and office personnel and completes over $900 million in revenue annually performing work across the United States. jobs.title: USAMRIID Antiviral Drug Discovery and Infectious Disease at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/14/2026 Reference Code USAMRDC-MRIID-2026-0008RHow to ApplyAll applications must be submitted through Zintellect at www.zintellect.comDescriptionThe Department of Defense (DoD) is offering a postdoctoral fellowship at the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command – Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRDC MRIID).What will I be doing? As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will engage in efforts to advance translational antiviral drug discovery. Research activities will include recombinant protein expression and purification, biochemical screening assay development, computational structural modeling, cell-based antiviral validation studies, and exposure to preclinical small-animal research models.Why Should I Apply? Under the guidance of a mentor, you will engage in research activities that include, but are not limited to: Designing, expressing, purifying, and characterizing recombinant viral and host proteins to support biochemical and structural studies. Applying computational tools to analyze protein structure and function, identify potential binding pockets, and map small-molecule interactions. Developing and using biochemical and cell-based assays to evaluate candidate antiviral compounds and investigate their mechanisms of action. Gaining experience with high-throughput phenotypic drug screening and anti-viral assays and applying promising therapeutic candidates in organoid and zebrafish disease models, with opportunities to support subsequent preclinical small-animal studies. Learning research that integrates protein science, computational analysis, and antiviral drug discovery with advanced disease models, including organoids and zebrafish, to evaluate promising therapeutic candidates. Where will I be located? Frederick, Maryland What is the anticipated start date? The USAMRIID is ready to make appointments immediately. Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and internships or fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified. What is the appointment length? Appointments are initially for one year with the option to extend the appointment for up to four additional years, contingent upon project needs and funding availability. What are the provisions? You will receive a stipend to be determined by MRIID. The stipend range for this opportunity is $70,000-$80,000/12-month appointment. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. Other provisions may include the following: • Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE) • Relocation Allowance • Training and Travel Allowance Security Clearance While participants will not enter an employment relationship with DoD or any other agency, this opportunity will require a suitability investigation/background investigation. Any offer made is considered tentative pending favorable outcome of the investigation.

jobs.title: 2027 Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program at Monarch Quantum
jobs.description: Employer: Monarch Quantum Expires: 11/14/2026 The Monarch Quantum Summer Internship Program offers students the opportunity to work on cutting‑edge technology shaping the future of quantum computing. Interns join multidisciplinary teams and contribute to real engineering projects that support our quantum hardware, software, and system‑level development efforts.As a Monarch intern, you may help design or test components, build experimental setups, develop control or automation software, analyze system performance, or support integration of quantum‑safe technologies—depending on your background and interests. Interns collaborate closely with experienced engineers and researchers while gaining hands‑on experience in a fast‑moving, industry‑focused environment.We encourage applications from students who are curious, motivated, and excited to apply their technical skills to emerging quantum technologies. Opportunities are available for students at the bachelor's, master’s and PhD levels.Some project examples include:Develop a test fixture for assessing the stability of opto-mechanical bonds & assemblies and perform stability experiments. The intern will define test goals & requirements, execute mechanical & optical design of a fixture and test station, facilitate material procurement, build the assembly, execute testing, compile results, and deliver a presentation to engineering leadership. The intern will also participate in ongoing projects to gain exposure in a professional, high precision engineering environment.Work hands-on with an optically pumped semiconductor laser (OPSL) system in an ISO-7 (Class 10,000) cleanroom laboratory, collaborating with and mentored by junior and senior engineers as well as senior management. Intern project opportunities in this role include, but are not limited to, material characterization; device-level semiconductor laser characterization such as spectral analysis and power-efficiency measurements; and optical and thermal modeling using tools such as Zemax, COMSOL, SolidWorks, and ANSYS. Interns will gain practical experience across the full development cycle, from simulation and design through laboratory testing and analysis.Contribute to the optical design of components and lenses for next‑generation laser modules. Interns will help develop and design test stations used to evaluate both individual components and full module assemblies. The role includes hands‑on intern involvement in building and operating these test stations to collect and analyze performance data. The intern will also support the development and validation of new design methodologies for laser module engineeringSupport the development of advanced automated pick‑and‑place routines for a fully integrated robotic cell consisting of multiple 6‑DOF industrial robots. The project includes designing, implementing, and testing motion control algorithms that improve accuracy, speed, and reliability of component handling within the automated cell. The intern will collaborate with robotics engineers to develop end‑to‑end workflows, including path planning, error detection, sensor integration, and automation sequencing. In addition, the intern will help evaluate system performance, optimize cycle times, and contribute to documentation and validation of the robotic software stack.Design a reliability test station for cutting-edge photonics components. Develop requirements, procure parts, and build a test system that allows a laser to auto-focus into a micron-sized target. Interns will utilize CAD software to design the test layout and work directly to set up the experiment in a cleanroom laser laboratory environment. They will write a script in python or LabView to perform the auto-focusing calibration routine.Work alongside experienced engineers to design, analyze, document, and test electrical systems and prototypes. Intern responsibilities include schematic development, PCB documentation, data analysis, test execution, and supporting failure analysis and corrective actions. This project provides extensive opportunities for technical skill-building, mentorship, and exposure to professional electrical engineering practices.Support the build and test of existing and novel External Cavity Diode Laser (ECDL) products through hands on lab experiments. Interns will join the laser development team and will design and execute tests to prove components and full laser assemblies to support Monarch Quantum's mission to deliver high-quality light engines to our customers. Project opportunities include building and characterizing laser cavities with novel components, designing diode test stations, improving alignment processes, and modeling laser systems. Interns will be mentored by collaborating with senior scientists, management, and laser technicians. Interns will leave the experience with a strong theoretical knowledge of and hands-on experience with ECDLs.Focus on developing FPGA-based systems using hybrid C/C++ and HDL architectures, including designing interfaces to ADCs, DACs, microcontrollers, and other components. Interns will support the creation and testing of advanced data acquisition and analysis systems, participate in hardware‑firmware integration, and contribute to reviews, verification, and documentation.Support the development of automated optical assembly processes, with a focus on investigating adhesive properties and performance when bonding precision optics to metal components. Interns will design and execute experiments to characterize adhesive behavior, develop and refine process parameters, and evaluate the impact on optical performance and assembly quality. They will also receive hands-on training in optical alignment, precision motion systems, and robotic automation. This project will provide practical experience at the intersection of optics, materials, process development, and robotics.

jobs.description: Employer: Siemens - Smart Infrastructure Expires: 11/15/2026 Building Automation Design Engineer InternshipLocation: San Francisco area office, located in Fremont, CAUndergraduate: Rising Sophomore, Rising Junior, Rising SeniorDuration: 10 weeks Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7 or June 14, 2027 Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/weekHere at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you? Who designs your future? You do.Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you?Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Building Automation Design Engineer Intern in Summer 2027! What is Building Automation?Siemens Building Automation Systems is a building management system (BMS) that automatically manages and controls all systems within a building. These systems include lighting, heating, cooling, ventilation, fire detection and notification, CCTV, door and window controls, water and waste management. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. The system is designed to manage a wide range of building systems, such as HVAC, lighting, security, fire safety, and other critical building functions. What you will do as a Building Automation Design Engineer InternThis internship is a 10 week program where you will rotate through various departments at the local Siemens office, all focusing on smart buildings and sustainable infrastructure. 80% of your time will be spent as a Design Engineer understanding the overall aspects of the role and related activities. 20% of your time with be spent with the Design Engineering Team Lead to understand the engineering role and engineering-related administrative tasksResponsibilities while working alongside our Engineering and Operations Teams include:Understanding project requirements and design build engineering solutions for higher education and K–12 education facilities, data centers, hospitals, pharmaceutical facilities, high-rise buildings, and lab facilities Preparing design documents, including system layouts, electrical drawings, bills of materials, sequences of operations, valve and damper schedules, and panel layouts as well as formatting and compiling submittals to Siemens L5 standard (unless established customer standard exists) Designing building network architecture to support operator workstations Analyzing plans, construction contract specifications, and codes to determine project requirements and risks Designing building and space pressurization solutions, chiller and boiler plant sequencing control, etc. Preparing engineering re-estimates and follow up with appropriate sales and management to ensure understanding of and satisfaction with job scope The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation.To apply for the Building Automation Design Engineer Internship Program, candidates must meet the following requirements:Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university Pursing an Engineering-related degree such as Electrical/Mechanical/Industrial Engineering, Construction Management, Computer – Aided Design and Drafting or related field of study Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August) Must be able to work on-site up to 3 days a week There is no relocation or housing stipend for this program Eligible candidate must be located within 50 miles of office location with access to a reliable vehicle, as this role does not provide transportation, housing or relocation support This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPTYou’ll win us over by having the following qualifications:Must be able to use hand tools, laptop, email, smartphone, and tablet Skilled in using Windows laptops and adept at learning new software related to building automation systems Ability to work in a team environment providing dedicated support to our customers Demonstrated leadership potential Strong analytical, writing, presentation and critical thinking skills Good verbal and written communication skills in English Experience or technical education in designing building automation (HVAC/lighting) projects with standard tools, products, and practices Experience or technical education utilizing AutoCAD As part of the application, you will be asked to confirm your enrollment status. jobs.title: (#R20054) User Experience Design Intern at American Electric Power
jobs.description: Employer: American Electric Power Expires: 11/16/2026 Job SummaryAs a User Experience Design Intern, you will join the User Experience team within AEP's Information Technology organization, creating effective digital experiences for customers, employees, and business partners. You will help make it easier for customers to do business with AEP and support customer-facing agents with clearer, more useful tools and workflows. Working with UX designers, researchers, product managers, developers, and business partners, you will gain hands-on experience contributing to meaningful enterprise projects across the user experience design lifecycle. The role emphasizes user research, experience strategy, journey mapping, service design, facilitation, wireframing, prototyping, and usability testing to help teams understand user needs and shape effective solutions. Projects may include web and mobile self-service, employee and agent tools, and responsible AI experiences such as conversational interfaces and intelligent assistance. Job DescriptionWhat You Will Do • Support discovery and research with customers, employees, agents, stakeholders, and subject matter experts to understand goals, needs, pain points, behaviors, and key tasks. • Help plan and facilitate interviews, workshops, co-creation sessions, design thinking activities, and other collaborative exercises. • Synthesize qualitative and quantitative research into themes, insights, opportunity areas, and recommendations that teams can act on. • Create or contribute to journey maps, service blueprints, personas, empathy maps, task flows, information architecture, and other experience design artifacts. • Create sketches, wireframes, and prototypes that help teams explore ideas, evaluate concepts, and communicate experience recommendations. • Help design and evaluate AI-enabled user experiences for customers and employees, including customer service agents.
